_desc: HOP_BUDGET chain gate — drive via tools/dm_diff_band.py --band 0 --funnel report --min-delivery full. A 6-hop chain alice -> r1 -> r2 -> r3 -> r4 -> r5 -> dave: the originator budget = min(31, rt_hops(6) + slack(3)) = 9; the five forwarders decrement (9->8->7->6->5->4); dave (the destination) is exempt -> delivered. LOAD-BEARING (review #02): the 6-hop length means a per-hop decrement scaled >=2x would exhaust the last forwarder r5 (9->7->5->3->1->-1 -> HOP_BUDGET NACK, no delivery) and a budget under-computed by >=5 would also fail -> either flips delivery to 0/1 and trips the band. What this gate does NOT assert is a SINGLE-off decrement (the +3 slack + exempt-dst keep a valid route delivering for any decrement in [0..1] per hop) — that exact per-hop value (hops_remaining/committed_hops on the forwarded DATA) is the UNIT tests' job (test_node_r3.cpp 'forwarder decrements'). Budget enforcement is purely SUBTRACTIVE (it only ever KILLS a delivery at a forwarder; the dst is always exempt), so no delivery-band gate can be tight on a single decrement; this gate proves delivery-NEUTRALITY on a valid route + catches gross budget/decrement regressions, identical lua-vs-meshroute. Not runnable directly (nodes carry no engine/script).
